findings.problem: Source-closed list/relation singleton deletion could exhaust analysis budget while oneMinimal remained true.
findings.originalReproduction: Writer P commits one identity; reader A returns the same identity with a different value. maxStates=0 keeps the direct anomaly, but deleting A produces a source-complete undecided history.
findings.fix: Undecided source-closed candidates are recorded and prevent a minimality claim. Source-missing deletions remain outside the source-closed predicate.

findings.problem: The v4 declared-register wrapper inherited oneMinimal from the legacy balanced reducer even when required singleton deletions were undecided.
findings.originalReproduction: Three transactions form an RW cycle and all write z without a declared z order. maxAttempts=0 leaves each source-closed singleton deletion undecided.
findings.fix: The new v4 wrapper independently rechecks final deletions within the remaining maxChecks budget and records unresolved candidates. Existing v3 behavior and evidence are unchanged.
independentChecks: declared register unknown singleton deletions prevent oneMinimal
adequate budgets still prove source-closed transaction minimality

findings.problem: Concurrent first directory creation could fail with FileExistsError.
findings.fix: Concurrent creation rechecks the directory and preparation is serialized by an OS lock.

findings.problem: Materialization could overwrite different bytes created after its final check.
findings.fix: Existing files are verified without replacement; publication is exclusive and non-overwriting.

findings.problem: A complete content-addressed blob set still required an archive ZIP for offline preparation.
findings.fix: Archives are opened lazily only for missing blobs.

findings.problem: Cache publication lacked a safe fallback on filesystems without hardlinks.
findings.fix: Serialized exclusive-copy fallback verifies the result and cleans its own partial publication after failures; unrelated files are preserved.

findings.problem: New package consumers added explicit timeout overrides beyond the original three allowed complete legacy suites.
findings.fix: 031, v4 and source preparation now use the unchanged 180-second default. Source consumers may reuse the declared public content-addressed cache while every input remains checksum-verified.

confirmedBoundaries.budgets: Verification and capsule replay require independent caller options; reports and digests do not grant higher budgets.
confirmedBoundaries.reductionModel: Reduction requires an explicit matching serializable or strict-serializable preservation target; captures/list/relation do not gain strict-model support.
confirmedBoundaries.classification: v4 category classification checks selected G0/G1c/G2-item categories for registers/lists; relation category classification remains explicitly unsupported.
confirmedBoundaries.sourceClosure: Missing captured writers remain visible coverage gaps; inferred orders are not promoted to capture observations.
confirmedBoundaries.evidenceIdentity: Schema, semantic contract, algorithm and counter identities bind replay; self-consistent forged digests cannot authorize a changed conclusion.
confirmedBoundaries.producerMetadata: Producer product version is metadata; semantic identifiers and recomputation determine support.
confirmedBoundaries.receiptCompression: Gzip stores the complete supplied receipt. The actual 9517-entry source fingerprint roundtrip preserved every field.
confirmedBoundaries.fingerprintCoverage: All non-artifacts frozen inputs are checked against pinned hashes; artifacts compatibility cache copies are excluded from the source map and executed dist is separately bound.
confirmedBoundaries.sourceConsumerCache: The fresh source consumer may reuse only checksum-pinned public input blobs. It rebuilds current compiled code from its extracted sources, with the external toolchain; it does not reuse author dist.
